title: 2 Kings Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who was Naaman in 2 Kings 5?
options: Captain of the host of the king of Syria
Prophet of Israel
King of Syria
Servant of Elisha
questions.correctAnswer: Captain of the host of the king of Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:1 states that Naaman was the captain of the host of the king of Syria.

questions.question: What disease did Naaman have?
options: Leprosy
Blindness
Paralysis
Fever
questions.correctAnswer: Leprosy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:1 says Naaman was a leper, meaning he had leprosy.

questions.question: Who was taken captive from Israel and served Naaman's wife?
options: A little maid
Naaman's sister
A prophet's daughter
A servant from Damascus
questions.correctAnswer: A little maid
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:2 tells us a little maid was taken captive from Israel and waited on Naaman's wife.

questions.question: What did the captive maid say she wished for Naaman?
options: That he were with the prophet in Samaria
That he had more wealth
That he would be a king
That he could return to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: That he were with the prophet in Samaria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:3 records that the maid wished her lord were with the prophet in Samaria who could heal him.

questions.question: What did the king of Syria send with Naaman to the king of Israel?
options: Ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment
Only a letter
Gold and a horse
A message and a servant
questions.correctAnswer: Ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:5 describes the king of Syria sending Naaman with ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment.

questions.question: What was the king of Israel's reaction to the letter from the king of Syria?
options: He rent his clothes in distress
He rejoiced and prepared a feast
He ignored the letter
He sent a reply immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes in distress
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:7 tells that upon reading the letter, the king of Israel rent his clothes and was distressed.

questions.question: What did Elisha tell the king of Israel after hearing about his reaction?
options: Let Naaman come to me, and he shall know there is a prophet in Israel
Ignore Naaman's request
Send gifts to the king of Syria
Prepare the army for war
questions.correctAnswer: Let Naaman come to me, and he shall know there is a prophet in Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:8 shows Elisha instructing the king to let Naaman come to him to prove there is a prophet in Israel.

questions.question: Where did Naaman stand when he came to Elisha's house?
options: At the door of the house of Elisha
Inside the house
On his chariot
In the city square
questions.correctAnswer: At the door of the house of Elisha
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:9 states that Naaman stood at the door of Elisha's house with his horses and chariot.

questions.question: What did Elisha send to Naaman instead of meeting him personally?
options: A messenger with instructions to wash in Jordan seven times
A letter asking for silver
A servant to carry out a sacrifice
Nothing, he met Naaman himself
questions.correctAnswer: A messenger with instructions to wash in Jordan seven times
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:10 records Elisha sending a messenger to tell Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times to be healed.

questions.question: True or False: Naaman immediately obeyed Elisha’s instruction to wash in the Jordan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:11-12 shows Naaman was angry and initially refused to wash in the Jordan as Elisha instructed.

questions.question: True or False: Naaman believed the rivers Abana and Pharpar were better than the waters of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:12 records Naaman questioning why he should wash in the Jordan instead of the rivers Abana and Pharpar of Damascus.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha accepted the gift offered by Naaman after he was healed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:16 shows Elisha refusing to accept a blessing or gift from Naaman after his healing.

questions.question: True or False: Gehazi, Elisha’s servant, ran after Naaman to receive gifts secretly.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:20 describes Gehazi deciding to run after Naaman to take something from him despite Elisha's refusal.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 5, which action comes first?
options: Naaman receives instructions to wash in the Jordan
The king of Israel rents his clothes
Naaman arrives at Elisha's house
The captive maid speaks about the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: The captive maid speaks about the prophet
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:3 shows the captive maid speaking about the prophet before the king of Israel rents his clothes (verse 7) or Naaman arrives (verse 9).

questions.question: What did the king of Syria ask the king of Israel to do with Naaman?
options: Recover him of his leprosy
Imprison him
Give him land
Make him a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Recover him of his leprosy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:6 records the king of Syria's letter asking the king of Israel to recover Naaman of his leprosy.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What instruction did Elisha give to Naaman for his healing?
options: Go and wash in Jordan seven times
Pray seven times in the house of the Lord
Offer a burnt sacrifice at the temple
Fast for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Go and wash in Jordan seven times
questions.explanation: Elisha sent a messenger to Naaman instructing him to wash seven times in the Jordan River to be cleansed of his leprosy, as recorded in 2 Kings 5:10. This instruction connects to Naaman's healing in verse 14 after he obeyed the command.

questions.question: How did Naaman initially react to Elisha's instruction to wash in the Jordan?
options: He was wroth and went away in anger
He immediately obeyed and washed
He asked for another river
He prayed for a sign
questions.correctAnswer: He was wroth and went away in anger
questions.explanation: Naaman was angry and displeased because he expected a more dramatic healing ritual. He went away in anger as recorded in 2 Kings 5:11, which shows his initial struggle with humility and obedience.

questions.question: Which rivers did Naaman compare to the waters of Israel as better for washing?
options: Abana and Pharpar
Euphrates and Tigris
Jordan and Kishon
Nile and Gihon
questions.correctAnswer: Abana and Pharpar
questions.explanation: Naaman questioned why he should wash in the Jordan when the rivers Abana and Pharpar, both rivers of Damascus, were better, as stated in 2 Kings 5:12. This comparison led to his initial rejection of Elisha’s instruction.

questions.question: What reasoning did Naaman's servants give to persuade him to obey the prophet's command?
options: If the prophet had asked him to do something great, he would have done it; so he should do this simple thing
The rivers of Israel were known for healing powers
Elisha was a powerful prophet, so his word was law
Obedience leads to blessings
questions.correctAnswer: If the prophet had asked him to do something great, he would have done it; so he should do this simple thing
questions.explanation: Naaman's servants reminded him that if the prophet had asked for something difficult, he would have done it, so he should obey the simple instruction to wash, as found in 2 Kings 5:13. This encouraged Naaman toward obedience.

questions.question: What was the result after Naaman dipped himself seven times in the Jordan as the prophet said?
options: His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean
Nothing happened initially
He fell ill after washing
He gained strength but not healing
questions.correctAnswer: His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean
questions.explanation: Upon obeying Elisha's instruction, Naaman's flesh was restored and he was cleansed of his leprosy, described in 2 Kings 5:14. This shows the blessing of faith and obedience.

questions.question: After his healing, what did Naaman acknowledge about God?
options: There is no God in all the earth, but in Israel
The God of Syria is the true God
All gods are equal
The God of Damascus healed him
questions.correctAnswer: There is no God in all the earth, but in Israel
questions.explanation: Naaman confessed that he now knew there was no God in all the earth except the God of Israel, as he said in 2 Kings 5:15. This declaration shows his recognition and faith in the true God.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when Naaman offered him a blessing?
options: He refused to accept any gift
He accepted the blessing gratefully
He asked for a portion of the silver
He requested Naaman to stay in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to accept any gift
questions.explanation: Elisha refused to receive a blessing or gift from Naaman, stating he would accept nothing, as recorded in 2 Kings 5:16. This shows Elisha’s integrity and reliance on God's provision.

questions.question: What did Naaman request regarding earth from Israel, and why?
options: Two mules' burden of earth, to offer sacrifices only to the LORD
Soil to plant trees in Syria
Earth to build an altar for Rimmon
A portion of Israel’s land as a gift
questions.correctAnswer: Two mules' burden of earth, to offer sacrifices only to the LORD
questions.explanation: Naaman asked for two mules' burden of earth from Israel because he would offer no burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, only to the LORD, as he explained in 2 Kings 5:17. This reflects his commitment to worship the true God.

questions.question: What condition did Naaman ask Elisha to pardon him for?
options: Bowing in the house of Rimmon when his master worships there
Not offering sacrifices in Israel
Keeping his leprosy hidden
Refusing to follow Elisha fully
questions.correctAnswer: Bowing in the house of Rimmon when his master worships there
questions.explanation: Naaman requested pardon for bowing in the house of Rimmon when his master worshipped there and he had to assist, as stated in 2 Kings 5:18. This shows his struggle to remain faithful despite his circumstances.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 5:14 promise will happen if the reader does what 2 Kings 5:10 instructs?
options: The flesh shall come again like unto a little child, and the person will be clean
The person will gain physical strength
The person will receive a prophetic vision
The person will be accepted by the king
questions.correctAnswer: The flesh shall come again like unto a little child, and the person will be clean
questions.explanation: Verse 10 instructs washing seven times in Jordan, and verse 14 confirms that doing so results in flesh being restored and cleansing of leprosy, showing the promise and power of obedience and faith in God's word.

questions.question: How does the passage from 2 Kings 5:11-13 teach us about humility in Christian living?
options: Naaman had to overcome pride and anger to obey a simple command
Naaman was immediately humble and obedient
Humility is unnecessary if one is a great man
Naaman ignored advice and was healed anyway
questions.correctAnswer: Naaman had to overcome pride and anger to obey a simple command
questions.explanation: These verses show Naaman’s initial anger and pride in rejecting the prophet’s instruction, but his servants' counsel helped him humbly obey, illustrating the importance of humility and submission in faith.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles to obey a simple instruction that seems beneath them. Based on 2 Kings 5, what biblical truth applies?
options: Obedience to God’s simple commands leads to blessing and healing
Only grand displays of faith are effective
God prefers sacrifices over obedience
Pride is a sign of spiritual strength
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s simple commands leads to blessing and healing
questions.explanation: Naaman’s story in 2 Kings 5:10-14 shows that humble obedience to God’s instructions, even if simple, leads to restoration, encouraging believers to trust and obey God in all things.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha accepted the gifts Naaman offered after his healing.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elisha refused to accept any gifts or blessings from Naaman, as recorded in 2 Kings 5:16, demonstrating his integrity and reliance on God rather than material gain.

questions.question: True or False: Naaman promised to worship no other gods but the LORD after his healing.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Naaman declared he would no longer offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to other gods but only to the LORD, as stated in 2 Kings 5:17, showing his commitment to exclusive worship of God.

questions.question: True or False: Naaman's servants advised him to reject the prophet’s instructions because they were too simple.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Naaman's servants encouraged him to obey the simple instruction of washing in Jordan, arguing that if he would do something greater, he should certainly do this, as found in 2 Kings 5:13.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 5.

questions.question: What was Gehazi's main motivation for following after Naaman after Elisha refused the gifts?
options: To offer Naaman a blessing
To receive something by deceit
To deliver a message from Elisha
To escort Naaman safely
questions.correctAnswer: To receive something by deceit
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:20 shows Gehazi's intent to take something from Naaman after Elisha refused the gifts, revealing his greed and deceit.

questions.question: How did Naaman respond when Gehazi approached him asking for gifts on behalf of Elisha's 'sons of the prophets'?
options: He refused to give anything
He gave one talent of silver only
He gave two talents of silver and two changes of garments
He sent a message instead of gifts
questions.correctAnswer: He gave two talents of silver and two changes of garments
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:23 states that Naaman gave two talents of silver and two changes of garments to Gehazi, showing his generosity despite not knowing Gehazi's true intent.

questions.question: What was Elisha's reaction when Gehazi returned with the gifts, pretending he had been nowhere?
options: He praised Gehazi for his loyalty
He asked Gehazi to confess his actions
He confronted Gehazi about his deceit and greed
He accepted the gifts on behalf of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: He confronted Gehazi about his deceit and greed
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:26 shows Elisha confronting Gehazi about his deceit, highlighting the moral lesson on honesty and the consequences of greed.

questions.question: What was the consequence Elisha pronounced on Gehazi because of his actions?
options: He would lose his prophetic gift
He would suffer Naaman's leprosy forever
He would be exiled from Israel
He would be struck down immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He would suffer Naaman's leprosy forever
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27 declares that Gehazi would bear Naaman's leprosy forever as punishment, illustrating the grave consequences of his sin.

questions.question: What did Naaman request from Elisha before departing, showing his newfound faith?
options: A healing for his wife
The gift of prophecy
A blessing from Elisha
A charge to worship other gods
questions.correctAnswer: A blessing from Elisha
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:15 shows Naaman asking Elisha to accept a blessing from him, acknowledging the God of Israel as the only true God.

questions.question: Why did Naaman want to take 'two mules' burden of earth' with him from Israel?
options: To build an altar in Syria
To offer sacrifices to the LORD on Syrian soil
To sell it in Damascus
To use it as a healing agent
questions.correctAnswer: To offer sacrifices to the LORD on Syrian soil
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:17 explains that Naaman wanted to take earth from Israel to worship the LORD there, symbolizing his commitment despite living in a foreign land.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when Naaman offered him a blessing and gifts?
options: He accepted the gifts with gratitude
He accepted only the blessing
He refused both gifts and blessing
He asked for more gifts
questions.correctAnswer: He refused both gifts and blessing
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:16 shows Elisha refusing to accept anything from Naaman, emphasizing that God's healing is a gift, not a commodity.

questions.question: Naaman expressed concern about bowing in the house of Rimmon because:
options: He feared the god Rimmon would curse him
He wanted to avoid offending the king of Syria
He feared losing his healing
He did not believe in Rimmon
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to avoid offending the king of Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:18 reveals Naaman's dilemma about bowing in the house of Rimmon to please his master, showing his struggle between faith and political loyalty.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently displayed in the story of Naaman's healing and Gehazi's deceit in 2 Kings 5?
options: Chiasm, highlighting reversal of fortunes
Alliteration, emphasizing key words
Parallelism, contrasting obedience and disobedience
Foreshadowing, predicting Israel’s exile
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism, contrasting obedience and disobedience
questions.explanation: The chapter uses parallelism by contrasting Naaman's obedience to Elisha's instructions with Gehazi's disobedience and greed (2 Kings 5:14 vs 5:20-27), emphasizing the moral lessons.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'leper' in this chapter primarily denotes which of the following?
options: A skin disease considered ritual impurity
An incurable mental illness
A physical disability affecting mobility
A contagious respiratory disease
questions.correctAnswer: A skin disease considered ritual impurity
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'tzaraath' used here refers to a skin condition that rendered one ritually unclean, as reflected in 2 Kings 5:1 and Leviticus 13, linking physical and spiritual impurity.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament passage is thematically connected to Naaman's story by emphasizing God's power to heal and cleanse leprosy?
options: Leviticus 13
Exodus 15
Numbers 12
Deuteronomy 28
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 13
questions.explanation: Leviticus 13 outlines the laws concerning leprosy and purification rituals, providing the background for understanding the significance of Naaman's healing (2 Kings 5:1-14).

questions.question: How does Naaman's healing prefigure New Testament themes regarding faith and humility?
options: It foreshadows the ministry of John the Baptist
It illustrates that faith in God's word brings healing, not human effort
It shows that only kings can receive God's blessings
It denies the need for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that faith in God's word brings healing, not human effort
questions.explanation: Naaman's reluctant obedience and ultimate cleansing (2 Kings 5:10-14) foreshadow New Testament teachings, such as in John 9:1-7, where faith and humility are necessary for healing.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's power being revealed through a foreigner, as in Naaman's story?
options: Matthew 5:3-12
Romans 12:1-2
Hebrews 11:1
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34-35 highlights that God shows no partiality but accepts those who fear Him from every nation, reflected in Naaman, a Syrian, receiving healing and acknowledging the God of Israel (2 Kings 5:15).

questions.question: True or False: Gehazi's punishment of leprosy was limited only to his lifetime and did not affect his descendants.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27 states that Gehazi's leprosy would cleave to him and his descendants forever, indicating a generational curse as a consequence of his sin.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha's refusal to accept gifts from Naaman demonstrates that God's grace cannot be bought.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:16 shows Elisha refusing gifts, illustrating the biblical principle that God's blessings are unmerited gifts, a theme echoed in Ephesians 2:8-9.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's sovereignty is revealed when the king of Israel tears his clothes upon receiving Naaman's letter?
options: God alone has power over life and death
Kings have ultimate authority over healing
Prophets can perform miracles by their own power
Leprosy is incurable by divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God alone has power over life and death
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:7 shows the king of Israel tearing his clothes and lamenting, 'Am I God, to kill and to make alive?' This expresses the doctrine that only God has sovereign power over life and death, not human rulers. This aligns with God's sovereignty discussed in Job 12:10.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily demonstrated through Elisha's command to Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan River for healing?
options: God's holiness
God's mercy
God's justice
God's omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy
questions.explanation: Elisha's instruction in 2 Kings 5:10 to wash in the Jordan seven times, resulting in Naaman's healing, reveals God's mercy in providing a means for restoration despite Naaman's leprosy.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Naaman's healing reflect the broader redemptive theme of inclusion of Gentiles in God's salvation plan?
options: Naaman, a Syrian, is healed and acknowledges the God of Israel
Only Israelites are shown to be healed in this chapter
Naaman rejects Israel's God in favor of his own gods
The chapter focuses solely on Israel's internal affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Naaman, a Syrian, is healed and acknowledges the God of Israel
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 5:15, Naaman declares there is no God but in Israel, showing Gentile inclusion in God's salvation plan, foreshadowing the New Testament Gentile mission (Acts 10:34-35).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about repentance and obedience can be drawn from Naaman’s initial anger and eventual obedience to Elisha’s command?
options: True healing requires submission to God's simple commands despite personal pride
Miracles occur only when elaborate rituals are performed
God demands sacrifices before granting healing
Obedience is unnecessary if faith is strong
questions.correctAnswer: True healing requires submission to God's simple commands despite personal pride
questions.explanation: Verses 11-14 show Naaman’s initial anger at the simplicity of washing, but upon obedience, he is healed, teaching that repentance involves humble submission to God’s word, not human expectations.

questions.question: What does Gehazi’s deceit and its consequences teach about the doctrine of sin and divine judgment?
options: Sin leads to immediate and lasting judgment
God overlooks minor sins of servants
Deceit is acceptable for good causes
Judgment only falls on kings and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to immediate and lasting judgment
questions.explanation: Gehazi’s deceit in verses 20-27 results in him being struck with Naaman’s leprosy, illustrating that sin brings severe and lasting divine judgment.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed when Elisha refuses to accept Naaman’s gift after healing him?
options: God’s grace
God’s wrath
God’s omniscience
God’s immutability
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace
questions.explanation: Elisha’s refusal in 2 Kings 5:16 to accept a gift reveals God’s grace—salvation and healing are unearned gifts, not commodities.

questions.question: What theological principle about the nature of God’s prophets can be inferred from Elisha’s message to the king of Israel after he tore his clothes?
options: Prophets act as God’s representatives to reveal His will
Prophets have independent power apart from God
Prophets are political leaders
Prophets perform miracles to gain wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets act as God’s representatives to reveal His will
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 5:8, Elisha tells the king that Naaman should come to him to know there is a prophet in Israel, indicating that prophets serve as God's mouthpieces revealing His will.

questions.question: What does Naaman’s request for two mule burdens of earth (2 Kings 5:17) signify about his understanding of worship and sanctification?
options: He desires a place to worship the LORD on Syrian soil
He wants to build a temple in Syria
He plans to offer sacrifices to Rimmon
He rejects the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He desires a place to worship the LORD on Syrian soil
questions.explanation: Naaman’s request in 2 Kings 5:17 shows his desire to continue worshiping Yahweh even outside Israel, reflecting the sanctification of place for true worship.

questions.question: How does Naaman’s confession in verse 15 relate to the doctrine of the exclusivity of the true God in biblical theology?
options: He acknowledges there is no God but in Israel
He worships multiple gods
He denies the existence of God
He adopts Syrian gods
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledges there is no God but in Israel
questions.explanation: Naaman’s statement in 2 Kings 5:15 that 'there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel' affirms the biblical doctrine of monotheism and exclusivity of Yahweh.

questions.question: What does the healing of Naaman teach about the role of faith and works in divine healing according to this chapter?
options: Obedience to God’s word, even when simple, is essential for healing
Faith alone without action heals
Works alone without faith heal
Human effort is sufficient for healing
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s word, even when simple, is essential for healing
questions.explanation: Naaman’s healing in 2 Kings 5:14 after obeying the simple act of washing shows that faith expressed through obedience to God's command is necessary for divine healing.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the healing of Naaman was merely a natural recovery and not a miracle. What does 2 Kings 5:10-14 actually teach about the nature of this healing?
options: The healing was a direct act of God through prophetic command
Naaman's recovery was due to the medicinal properties of the Jordan
The healing was a coincidence
Naaman never had leprosy
questions.correctAnswer: The healing was a direct act of God through prophetic command
questions.explanation: Verses 10-14 describe Elisha’s prophetic command and Naaman’s obedience resulting in instantaneous healing, affirming a divine miracle rather than natural recovery.

questions.question: What does Gehazi’s punishment teach about the principle of corporate responsibility and generational consequences in the Old Testament?
options: Sin can bring consequences upon one’s descendants
Only the individual is punished for sin
God does not punish servants
Punishment is limited to this life
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can bring consequences upon one’s descendants
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27 states Gehazi’s leprosy will cleave unto him and his seed forever, reflecting Old Testament teaching on generational consequences of sin (Exodus 20:5).

questions.question: How does Naaman’s experience illustrate the doctrine of sanctification as a process involving God's initiative and human response?
options: God initiates healing and Naaman responds in obedience and worship
Sanctification is only human effort
Healing is random and unrelated to sanctification
God requires sacrifices before sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: God initiates healing and Naaman responds in obedience and worship
questions.explanation: Naaman’s healing (2 Kings 5:14) demonstrates God’s initiative in healing and Naaman’s response in obedience and later worship (2 Kings 5:15-18), illustrating sanctification's cooperative dynamic.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's providence can be derived from the role of the captive maid in Naaman’s healing narrative?
options: God uses the lowly and unexpected to bring about His purposes
Only kings can influence God's will
Captives have no role in God's plan
Healing depends on royal decree
questions.correctAnswer: God uses the lowly and unexpected to bring about His purposes
questions.explanation: The little maid in 2 Kings 5:2-3, though a captive servant, directs Naaman’s healing, showing God's providence in using humble instruments to fulfill His plans (cf. 1 Corinthians 1:27).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine grace and human integrity emerges from contrasting Elisha’s refusal of gifts and Gehazi’s greed?
options: True grace is freely given and must not be exploited for personal gain
God's gifts should be bartered for wealth
Prophets should accumulate riches
Greed is acceptable for God’s servants
questions.correctAnswer: True grace is freely given and must not be exploited for personal gain
questions.explanation: Elisha’s refusal of gifts (2 Kings 5:16) contrasts with Gehazi’s deceit and greed (2 Kings 5:20-26), teaching that divine grace is free and must be honored with integrity.
